## NS.tprintRaw() method

Prints a ReactNode to the terminal.

**Signature:**

```typescript
tprintRaw(node: ReactNode): void;
```

## Remarks

RAM cost: 0 GB

See the [ReactNode](./bitburner.reactnode.md) type for the acceptable values.

To render a raw HTML string, use [dangerouslySetInnerHTML](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/common#dangerously-setting-the-inner-html)<!-- -->.

Be careful when processing untrusted HTML strings. You should read the linked documentation carefully.

It's generally safe to use strings generated by the game (e.g., the string you get when using [read](./bitburner.ns.read.md) with .lit files), but do not trust arbitrary HTML strings. With untrusted HTML strings, you should sanitize them first with a library such as [DOMPurify](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify) or [HTML Sanitizer API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTML_Sanitizer_API) (remember to check whether your browser supports this API).

## Example


```js
ns.tprintRaw(123);
ns.tprintRaw("foo");
const safeHtmlString = ns.read("foo.lit");
ns.tprintRaw(React.createElement("div", { dangerouslySetInnerHTML: { __html: safeHtmlString } }));
const unsafeHtmlString = "<div>bar</div>";
// Do not do this
// ns.tprintRaw(React.createElement("div", { dangerouslySetInnerHTML: { __html: unsafeHtmlString } }));
// Assuming DOMPurify is imported
const sanitizedHtmlString = DOMPurify.sanitize(unsafeHtmlString);
ns.tprintRaw(React.createElement("div", { dangerouslySetInnerHTML: { __html: sanitizedHtmlString } }));
```

```jsx
const safeHtmlString = ns.read("foo.lit");
// This uses JSX syntax, which is only available in jsx and tsx script files.
ns.tprintRaw(<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: safeHtmlString }} />);
```
